prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #1597 fixes the architectural root cause: validation belongs at discovery time (`_handle_protected_resource_response`), not at every call to `get_resource_url()`. prs.title: fix: isolate streamable HTTP request errors
prs.author: he-yufeng
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP client POST requests hang forever when the server returns an error or the connection fails, because no JSON-RPC error response is written back to the caller. All three PRs fix this by converting failure conditions into a JSONRPCError sent to read_stream_writer: #1578 catches network/connection crashes inside _handle_post_request; #2613 replaces raise_for_status() with explicit HTTP 4xx/5xx handling (and includes test coverage with HTTP status in the error data field); #2607 wraps the handle_request_async dispatch closure in a broad try/except that would catch both of those failure modes plus any other exception from _handle_resumption_request. (3 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP client POST requests hang forever when the server returns an error or the connection fails, because no JSON-RPC error response is written back to the caller. prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2607 operates at the highest level — it wraps the task-dispatch closure that calls both _handle_post_request and _handle_resumption_request, making it a superset of #1578 (connection errors) and functionally equivalent to catching the raise_for_status() exception that #2613 eliminates. members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP client POST requests hang forever when the server returns an error or the connection fails, because no JSON-RPC error response is written back to the caller. All three PRs fix this by converting failure conditions into a JSONRPCError sent to read_stream_writer: #1578 catches network/connection crashes inside _handle_post_request; #2613 replaces raise_for_status() with explicit HTTP 4xx/5xx handling (and includes test coverage with HTTP status in the error data field); #2607 wraps the handle_request_async dispatch closure in a broad try/except that would catch both of those failure modes plus any other exception from _handle_resumption_request. (3 PRs)

members.cluster_pick_reason: #2607 operates at the highest level — it wraps the task-dispatch closure that calls both _handle_post_request and _handle_resumption_request, making it a superset of #1578 (connection errors) and functionally equivalent to catching the raise_for_status() exception that #2613 eliminates. Closing #1578 and #2613 in favor of #2607 avoids redundant catch layers. One important caveat: #2613 includes explicit tests and surfaces the HTTP status_code in the error data, which should be ported into #2607 before merge.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #1597 fixes the architectural root cause: validation belongs at discovery time (`_handle_protected_resource_response`), not at every call to `get_resource_url()`. By validating once on receipt and storing only trusted metadata, the guard in `get_resource_url()` becomes unnecessary regardless of URL normalization quirks. PR #2590 only patches the normalization symptom while leaving the structurally misplaced check in place; any future URL variant could trigger the same class of false-negative again.

members.title: fix: validate PRM resource field per RFC 9728 Section 3.3
members.author: bjoaquinc
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix incorrect behavior in `get_resource_url()` when the PRM (Protected Resource Metadata) provides a `resource` field. PR #1597 removes the `check_resource_allowed` guard from `get_resource_url()` and moves RFC 9728 §3.3 validation to `_handle_protected_resource_response()` (fail-fast at discovery time). PR #2590 keeps the guard but adds `_normalize_resource_url()` to strip trailing slashes so the guard no longer rejects semantically identical URLs. Both diffs produce mutually exclusive edits on the same lines of `get_resource_url()` and cannot both be merged. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2243 fixes the root cause automatically inside _resolve_endpoint_url without requiring callers to supply a new parameter, and its diff is self-contained to the resolution logic. PR #2531's fallback (messages_url=None) still calls plain urljoin and therefore leaves the gateway-prefix bug intact for all existing callers; the fix only applies when the caller already knows the correct URL and passes it in manually. Both PRs introduce an identically-named function with incompatible signatures, so they cannot coexist. The automatic detection approach in #2243 is the more complete fix; #2531's messages_url override concept could be added on top of #2243 in a follow-up if explicit override capability is still wanted.

clusters.pick_reason: #2514 is the superset fix: it adds the affirmative spec requirement (send notifications/cancelled via CancelledNotificationParams) and covers both timeout and caller-cancellation paths, making the error-response code that #2493 targets redundant. #2493 only removes incorrect behavior without fulfilling the outbound notification obligation, so merging #2514 renders #2493 unnecessary.

members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: RequestResponder.cancel() violated the MCP spec in two ways: it sent an error response for cancelled requests (forbidden by spec) and it omitted the required notifications/cancelled outbound message. Both PRs modify the same cancel() method in session.py — #2493 removes the illegal error-response path, #2514 adds the required CancelledNotification send. They are two halves of the same spec compliance fix and would conflict if both were merged.
